notes: Both joined locations opened. ur_kin.h:90 documents the IK joint solutions as 'all angles should be in [0,2*PI)' — a range whose 2*PI bound denotes radians. ur_kin.cpp:6-11 opened as well: the same joint values are passed directly to sin()/cos() (double s1 = sin(*q), c1 = cos(*q), ... q234), and C-library trig arguments are radians. Caveat disclosed: neither cited line contains the literal token 'rad'; the verdict rests on the [0,2*PI) range notation plus the sin/cos usage, which together state joint angles in radians.
